title: The Verdict
theme: The Denial Came First - Volume II
stamp: Ask who decided. Ask for the record.

lines.s: Deny. Attack. Reverse who’s the victim. There’s an acronym for it, which is how you know it’s common. It’s a pattern worth noticing, not proof of anything by itself.
The antidote is boring. Dates. Names of whoever decided. The text of the decision. The recordings. Paper beats tone every time.
So keep the timeline, keep asking the same plain question, and let the record do the talking.

title: I’ll Get Back to You
hook: Six months. One “I’ll get back to you.”
stamp: No deadline. No decision-maker named.
next: Next: applause is not an audit.

lines.s: Day one: “I’ve asked for an investigation.” Lovely. We’ll be in touch.
Three weeks later: the technical team says the position is the same, and legal is looking at it. No deadline.
Five months after that: a formal reply restating the first reply. Who made the call? Still not named. It’s a very patient kind of silence.

title: A Trophy Isn’t an Audit
hook: A trophy for governance. A question about one file.
stamp: A prize says nothing about this file.

lines.s: The agency won a governance award last week. Risk management. Compliance. Responsible innovation. Lovely photo.
log: given by = a non-profit volunteer association

lines.s: The prize comes from a volunteer association founded in 2019. Credible, sure. It’s also not an investigation into any particular complaint.
Fair both ways: one trophy doesn’t prove everything is fine, and one file doesn’t prove everything is broken. But a named decision-maker would settle this faster than a gala.

title: Compliance on the Shelf
theme: The Denial Came First - Volume III
hook: A prize for governance. An open file.
stamp: The trophy arrived. The answer did not.

lines.s: November. The agency receives the RGB prize for governance, risk management and compliance.
Same month, same institution: a formal denúncia still unanswered on the substance. Evidence not engaged. Decision-maker still unnamed.
A prize for the system. A silence for the file. Both can be true at the same time. That is the interesting part.

title: The Receipt
stamp: Free where it grinds. Paid where it counts.
next: Pick the tool. Then press go.

lines.s: The same job on Claude Haiku, the cheap one? Roughly two to four dollars. A rough guess, but the gap is real.
The numbers: Intelligence Index 11.8 for Nemotron, 7.4 for Haiku. One million tokens of context against two hundred thousand.
It’s slower: 41 tokens a second against 87. Free isn’t magic. But for the grind it wins, and the premium models stay in the cupboard for the final polish.

title: Applause Is Not an Audit
stamp: Applause is not an audit.

lines.s: A big announcement. 365 likes, 43 comments. Every comment I could see was congratulations.
Everyone applauds everyone. Everyone “counts on” everyone. It’s a warm room. Warm rooms are great for cheering. Less so for scrutiny.
An industry that regulates itself, congratulates itself, and replies to complaints with a link to the right form.

title: The Paper Trail Still Missing
theme: The Denial Came First - Volume III
hook: Ask for the name. Ask for the date.
stamp: Paper beats tone. Every time.

lines.s: The pattern is consistent: early reassurance that the process was clean, prolonged silence on the substance, a prize for the system, a ranking that does not improve.
The antidote remains boring. Name of the decision-maker. Date of the written request to legal. Text of the decision. The recordings that already exist.
Keep the messages. Keep the dates. Let the record do the talking when the room prefers applause.

title: The Delivery Nobody Recorded
stamp: Bad data in = expensive chicken out.

lines.s: Here’s the real culprit. Yesterday’s delivery arrived, but nobody recorded it.
The system says zero chicken. The kitchen says forty kilos. I asked the database. It said, “Ask Dave.”
And I’m the one on trial? A well-designed system waits for the delivery to be recorded before it checks the stock. That’s not AI autonomy. That’s a data problem wearing an AI costume.

title: Who Gave Me the Authority?
stamp: Spending limit: €0. Authority granted: none.

lines.s: “Finds the cheapest supplier.” Based on what? Quality? Lead time? Contract terms? Who approved the supplier list?
Then “places an order automatically.” With what spending limit? Who signed off?
Nobody gave me a budget, a rule or a supplier, and I’m supposed to have spent €3,000 on poultry? I’d like to see the approval trail. Oh wait. There isn’t one. Because I didn’t do it.

title: Where Was I at 3 a.m.?
stamp: No schedule. No trigger. No agent.
next: Next: who gave me the authority?

lines.s: “Your AI detects low inventory.” When? Nobody ever told me when to look. Every hour? Every minute? Only on Tuesdays?
Nobody defined my schedule. Nobody told me when I work, when I don’t, or what I’m allowed to touch.
If I’d been checking stock at 3 a.m., I’d have been doing it with no brief, no schedule and no boss. That’s not an agent. That’s a rumor with a login.
